items.definition: Able to break down naturally in the soil or water without harming the environment.
examples: The café has replaced plastic cups with biodegradable ones.

items.definition: The amount of carbon dioxide that a person, company or activity produces.
examples: Cycling to work is one way to reduce your carbon footprint.

items.definition: The cutting down of large areas of forest, so that the land can be used for something else.
examples: Deforestation in the Amazon destroys the homes of thousands of species.

items.definition: A long period with very little or no rain, when there is not enough water.
examples: The summer drought left many reservoirs almost empty.

items.definition: Gases or other substances that are sent into the air, especially by vehicles and factories.
examples: The city wants to cut emissions from traffic by a third.

items.definition: Of an animal or plant, at risk of disappearing completely from the wild.
examples: The Iberian lynx was once one of the most endangered cats in the world.

items.definition: The slow rise in the temperature of the Earth, caused mainly by pollution from human activity.
examples: Scientists link the melting of glaciers to global warming.

items.definition: The natural place where an animal or plant normally lives.
examples: New roads have destroyed the natural habitat of many birds.

items.definition: A large area where rubbish is buried under the ground, or the method of getting rid of rubbish this way.
examples: Most of our household waste still ends up in landfill.

items.definition: Produced without artificial chemicals, such as fertilisers or pesticides.
examples: We buy organic vegetables from a farm near our village.

trap.en: Ecological means connected with the relationship between living things and their environment. Food grown without chemicals is organic.
trap.es: Un «tomate ecológico» es an organic tomato. Ecological se usa para hablar del equilibrio entre seres vivos y su entorno, no de comida.

items.definition: Harmful substances in the air, water or soil that make them dirty or dangerous.
examples: Air pollution is a serious problem in many large cities.

items.definition: To treat used materials, such as paper or glass, so that they can be used again.
examples: We recycle all our glass bottles and cardboard.

items.definition: Of energy or resources, able to be replaced naturally, so they never run out.
examples: Wind and solar are the cheapest forms of renewable energy.

items.definition: Able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment or using up natural resources.
examples: The company wants to build more sustainable homes using local timber.

items.definition: Animals and plants that live naturally in the wild, not kept by people.
examples: The national park is famous for its wildlife.
